Approaching $x=-1$ from the left, we have $x<-1,$ so we use the expression $f(x)=2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi (x+1))-5.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to (-1)^{-}}f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to (-1)^{-}}[2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi (x+1))-5] \\  & =2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi (-1+1))-5 \\  & =2\operatorname{sin}⁡(0)-5 \\  & =-5.\end{aligned}
$$

On the other hand, approaching $x=2$ from the right, we have $x\ge 2,$ so we use the expression $f(x)=\sqrt{x-2}+(x-2)^{2}-3.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {2}^{+}}f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to {2}^{+}}(\sqrt{x-2}+(x-2)^{2}-3) \\  & =\sqrt{2-2}+(2-2)^{2}-3 \\  & =\sqrt{0}+{0}^{2}-3 \\  & =-3.\end{aligned}
$$
